title: Print Queue lifecycle reaper, attempt caps, chunking, and cooperative cancellation

acceptanceCriteria.description: Queue-send execution owns a durable generation and chunk claim, heartbeats while active, observes cooperative cancellation between orders, and rejects overlapping or stale executors before they can write progress.

The periodic reaper atomically leases interrupted or stale work, increments the durable generation, and parks poison items after three attempts and parent jobs after their bounded recovery budget instead of crash-looping.

A 1,000-order migrated-database certification runs as fifty sequenced chunks of twenty with concurrency four, produces 999 exactly-once queued outcomes, parks one poison order after three attempts, and records zero double sends.

Provider-pending work is never blindly replayed: exact durable receipts and shipment artifacts may resume only the bounded local persistence tail, while ambiguous, missing, invalid, or inconsistent effects remain held with provider dispatch disabled.

The card-required PS-400, PS-401 mixed-success, PS-403 worker recovery, PS-420 progress, durable queue, and PS-053 atomic recovery guards all pass at the reviewed SHA, along with strict TypeScript and the production web build.

The shipped-data override is narrow and documented. Existing shipped/cancelled edit locks, read-only UI gates, inventory kill switch, orders/shipments schemas, provider one-effect fences, and fail-closed label behavior were not weakened; verification performed no live label purchase, postage charge, marketplace notification, or production order/shipment mutation.

Migration 0073 was applied before runtime deployment, all fourteen sidecar objects are present, the exact reviewed SHA is live on the Render API, sync worker, and Print Queue worker, and Vercel has a Ready production deployment built from that exact SHA with healthy API readiness and Print Queue worker telemetry.

sotBypass.details: Durable backend rows and provider-operation receipts remain authoritative. Routes, provider adapters, and React do not calculate recovery eligibility, mint provider truth, rank rates, or authorize a second label purchase.

evidence.proves: The migrated PGlite workflow enforces exact generation/chunk claims and completes a 1,000-order parent as fifty bounded chunks with 999 queued, one terminal poison item, and zero duplicate effects.

Deterministic interruption, expired-heartbeat, overlapping generation, stale completion, timeout cancellation, and poison-order faults recover through the reaper without a second executor or an unbounded retry loop.

Fake-provider adversarial cases hold ambiguous operations, recover exact durable receipts once, reject stale or inconsistent shipment facts, and leave the provider mutation spy untouched during reconciliation.

caveats.description: The failure-injection suite interrupts the durable execution boundary deterministically instead of killing a production OS process. Exact-SHA worker restart, migration readiness, heartbeat, and reaper startup were then verified from live service logs without risking a real label or customer order.

The aggregate deep endpoint remains degraded because two order-sync accounts are stale or failed. This condition predates and is outside PS-452; Print Queue worker, fulfillment outbox, database, order reads, and event loop are healthy, so it does not block the Print Queue lifecycle release.
caveats.followUpTask: Investigate the two stale order-sync accounts independently without mutating shipped/cancelled order history.
